title: Cross-cohort acceptance driver for hybrid FP8/INT8 rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We lack an automated, cohort-aware acceptance driver that exercises candidate FP8/INT8 quantization profiles across realistic traffic slices and produces a single pass/fail decision plus a prioritized failure breakdown. Current golden checks only run on a single canonical corpus and miss cohort-specific regressions and skewed query distributions. Goal: implement a cross-cohort acceptance driver that (1) runs golden prompt families grouped by customer/cohort, (2) computes weighted multi-metric scores (semantic similarity, generation divergence, token-level logprob drift, hallucination signal), (3) enforces stage gates with per-cohort thresholds and a global stability window, and (4) emits structured artifacts (report, diffs, telemetry) consumable by rollout automation. Success criteria: a) Driver can evaluate a candidate profile across N=5 cohort slices in <60 minutes for a full golden run at 8k context, b) Pass/fail decisions match manual QA for 95% of sampled rollouts during the trial period, c) Telemetry dashboards show cohort-level delta and ranked root causes for top 3 failures, d) Driver integrates with rollout engine to block canary promotion when gate is failed. Scope: build the driver, define cohort weighting policy, implement metric computations, add a short-run smoke check and full-run mode, export results to Console and to a bucket for archival. Out of scope: customer-facing UI changes and long-retention analytics (handled by a follow-up).

QA checklist added: run smoke, run full, compare to baseline logits, inspect top hallucinatory outputs, sign off in comments.
pass_criteria: Global: weighted_score >= 0.92 where weighted_score = sum_i (cohort_weight_i * cohort_score_i)
Per-cohort: semantic_similarity_mean >= 0.88 (embedding cosine on anchor responses) for all cohorts
Per-cohort: generation_divergence (BLEU/ROUGE-lite) relative delta <= 6% compared to baseline profile
Token-level: median per-token logprob delta >= -0.15 (i.e., not a large confidence collapse), and 95th percentile delta >= -0.5
Hallucination: hallucination_rate <= 1.5% across golden QA prompts (uses ENG-582000 classifier), and any cohort with hallucination_rate > 2.5% fails immediately
Stability: must pass full-run gate 3 times in a row (full-run = complete golden family across all cohorts) within a 48h window to allow promotion
Smoke-run tolerance: a short smoke-run may exceed up to two metric thresholds but full-run must satisfy all criteria
failure_modes: Cohort skew: low-volume cohort shows >10% divergence but global weighted_score still passes — causes masked failure for that customer segment
Cache cold-start: quant candidate causes KV cache warming differences that inflate token-delta metrics on first two runs
Non-deterministic sampling: stochastic decoding differences cause noisy BLEU-style metrics — must run with deterministic seeds for acceptance runs
Classifier drift: hallucination classifier false positives on newly introduced prompt templates; flagged as false alarm unless baseline shows improvement
Metric sensitivity: overly tight per-token thresholds will block profiles that are cost-beneficial; thresholds may be tuned after trial
runbook_steps: 1) Kick off: Submit candidate profile via /internal/quant-acceptance API with param mode=smoke or mode=full
2) Runner provisions isolated GPU pool (per SRE isolation policy) and pins baseline and candidate models
3) Runner builds cohort slices (names: enterprise, searchbot, comms, support, misc) and fetches golden families from GCS
4) Execute smoke-run (subset of families) to catch regressions quickly; abort if any cohort has hallucination_rate > 5%
5) If smoke-run passes, execute full-run (all golden families). Persist per-query artifacts (baseline/candidate outputs, logits, embeddings) to results bucket
6) Compute metrics and aggregate with cohort weights. Produce JSON report and an HTML summary in results bucket. POST results to Console webhook and to rollout engine endpoint
7) If gate fails: mark candidate as blocked, convert report into a Jira-style action list and notify owners. If gate passes stability window, mark candidate as promotable
8) On failure, follow remediation steps: run targeted golden replay for failing cohort, instrument additional logging, consider local quantization re-calibration or layer-exclusion re-run
9) Rollback guard: ensure canary traffic remains on baseline until three consecutive full-run passes and human sign-off (PM or Eng lead)
10) Post-rollout: schedule 7-day monitoring job to detect slow drift and file follow-up if regressions appear
